placed.label: fig:dd-backend-change
placed.promise: What happens to a claim and its dependent text when the evidence or source changes?
placed.caption: Conceptual account of the current Writing App owner mechanism. A source passage, interpreted result and canonical claim retain separate identities. A human or agent proposes a change against an inspected revision. The owning operation checks authority and the expected basis, records the accepted transition and exposes affected dependencies for review. Work and history retain the request, outcome and recovery route. A current source pin establishes which bytes were used, not whether a source entails a claim. Scientific support is an authored judgement supplemented by scoped numerical, formal and independent review evidence where available. The same owners serve browser and agent interfaces. This diagram describes an implemented workflow principle, not an automatic theorem-proving or fully self-improving SDK.

placed.label: fig:dd-operator-projection
placed.promise: Does a small scalar gradient mean that the operator variation is small?
placed.caption: Archived classical calculations from the operatorial-loss prototype, seed 20240603 and 2000 samples per point. (a) Variance of the scalar gradient g decreases with qubit number n. (b) The recorded normalised operator-gradient fraction r_op remains near one half. Error bars in (b) are the archived sample standard deviations, not standard errors or confidence intervals. Local and global observable ensembles nearly coincide in this particular experiment. The result contrasts projected scalar feedback with retained operator content. It does not demonstrate that this operator can be measured or optimised at no additional cost.

placed.label: fig:dd-gap-selection
placed.promise: Which omitted direction most improves the retained ground-state calculation?
placed.caption: Archived reduced-space comparison from the residual-method prototype. lambda scales the declared coupling and E_P-E_0 is the retained-space ground-energy error, both in the model's dimensionless units. Each method adds one direction from the same candidate pool. Selecting by raw residual amplitude chooses a high-gap channel, while the producer's amplitude-over-gap rule selects a more useful low-gap channel. The resulting finite-model error is substantially lower. This is not a hardware test or proof that every gap-aware enlargement converges.

placed.label: fig:dd-memory-parity
placed.promise: Can a small continuation rule answer exact queries without scanning every unique world?
placed.caption: Retaining a relation rather than its list of instances. (a) Mathematical three-bit even-parity example under a uniform source law. Every pair of bits is independent, but two bits jointly determine the third. A running parity state suffices to represent allowed continuations. (b) Archived measurements for the 19-bit law with 262144 unique worlds, queries fixing four prefix coordinates and batch size Q. t_API is warm full-API time per batch. Small dots are all eleven samples and lines connect medians, not fitted scaling laws. Build, query preparation and process-first compilation are excluded. The same campaign records refusal for high-width laws and direct-scan wins on a duplicate-heavy control.

placed.label: fig:dd-superarc-controls
placed.promise: How much of the recorded score separation survives common answer-format treatment?
placed.caption: Archived SuperARC campaign decomposition, N=100 twelve-term binary targets. (a) rho_k is the fraction in each correct-answer class. All three arms were recorded correct under the campaign's distinct correctness routes, but the bare arm is mostly in the penalised print-type class. (b) Delta phi compares loop and execute/fix arms. Removing commentary with the class assignments held fixed removes the positive separation. Horizontal intervals are the retained report's 95 percent paired-bootstrap bands at resample size100, seed20260804,100resamples. The re-binned point has no interval reported here. Scores concern formula text, while A2/A3 correctness used banked program execution. Prompt, search and format differences prevent these increments from isolating causal execution or recursion benefits. Replotted from archived report objects and the skeptic's explicitly transcribed control tables, not a new experiment.

placed.label: fig:dd-retention-memory
placed.promise: Why can two identical coarse descriptions predict different futures, and what should be retained?
placed.caption: A mathematical illustration of task-relative retention. Four states exchange probability at the labelled symmetric rates. We ask only for the total probability in region A. Starting in state 1 or state 2 gives the same coarse answer, p_A=1, but different initial rates, -1 and -3. Retaining the imbalance z=(p_1-p_2)-(p_3-p_4) closes the prediction for y=p_A-p_B: y'=-4y+2z and z'=2y-12z. Eliminating z instead produces an exact memory term. This constructed example illustrates the projection and residual mechanisms developed in Foundations of Synthetics and Memory in Pieces. It is not an empirical performance result.

placed.label: fig:dd-shared-register-price
placed.promise: When should two minimisers stop sharing a register?
placed.caption: Mathematical illustration of the shared-register model. (a) Two tasks prefer a and b, while their equally weighted quadratic compromise is q*=(a+b)/2. (b) Optimised fixed-register loss L_B* and partition-enabled loss L_C* versus disagreement angle theta, with gamma=1, eta=0.8 and partition price C_part=0.25 in the source's dimensionless loss units. Separation becomes cheaper at theta=0.8411 rad, before the fixed-register optimum sacrifices a task at theta=1.0853 rad. The data are analytic model values from the retained illustration run, not measured performance.

placed.label: fig:dd-global-local-feedback
placed.promise: How can local and global objectives share an optimum but give different feedback?

For independent uniform angles, Var(partial_j C_G)=(1/8)(3/8)^(n-1), whereas Var(partial_j C_L)=1/(8n^2). n is the number of qubits. These curves are exact values in that model, not hardware measurements or a general convergence guarantee.

placed.label: fig:dd-memory-mechanism
placed.promise: What is retained, how is it queried, and where does refinement enter in the original and extended memory systems?
placed.caption: Two routes from sources to a reconstructed answer. Corpus as a State retains geometric summaries and inherited approximation bounds. Memory in Pieces, developed through Skein and Parallax, retains task/law coordinates, reconstruction and discarded-feedback diagnostics. Source-card extraction is model-dependent, while retention, decoding and declared bounds are mechanical conditional on those choices. A failed capacity or residual check triggers refinement or source-level fallback. Final language-model composition is separate from the retained numerical object.

placed.label: fig:dd-spectral-window
placed.promise: What does a Gaussian spectral filter retain, and what measurement resource does finer resolution demand?
placed.caption: Mathematical schematic for a self-adjoint H, real probe energy E_star and tau > 0, not a measured spectrum. Vertical marks represent possible energies. The Gaussian window has width proportional to tau^(-1/2). Its Fourier representation uses real-time evolution with typical time scale proportional to sqrt(tau), in units with hbar=1. Narrower energy resolution therefore requires longer-time information. ITQDE supplies an overlap-based construction and Free Snacks asks when the supported bandwidth can be treated locally. State support, quadrature error, denominator conditioning and measurement noise remain separate costs.

placed.label: fig:dd-register-phase-diagram
placed.promise: At which disagreement and register price is it optimal to share, split or suppress one evaluator?
placed.caption: Optimisation phase diagram for gamma=1 and eta=0.8. Below C_crit(theta), separate registers retain both tasks. Above it, balanced sharing is optimal at small disagreement, while a shared register suppresses one evaluator at large disagreement. Solid curves mark equal-cost choices. The dashed C_part=0.25 slice recovers the earlier crossing at theta=0.8411. The meeting point is theta=1.0853, C_part=0.4. Analytic finite-model regions, not measured thermodynamic phases.

Detailed content and its linked evidence are exposed through a readable summary, exact identity, state and permitted operations. Reading projects observations from the interior to the containing task. Writing narrows an outer request through the action interface to a local change. A readable digest summarises meaning, while a revision digest identifies the consumed version.

placed.label: fig:dd-nested-work-sdk
placed.promise: How do nested objects and parent-child tasks control context and acceptance, and what should an SDK preserve?
placed.caption: The same boundary pattern at different task altitudes. A parent sends a scoped question and relevant context to a worker. Source, calculation and claim remain distinct local objects, and an independent reviewer inspects the returned contribution. The parent consumes the findings before accepting its own result. A changed consumed input marks affected acceptance for attention. The dashed panel locates the SDK direction: reusable transition templates, configurable session topology and source modules governed through the same inspectable interfaces.

placed.label: fig:dd-hierarchy-stability
placed.promise: How does hierarchical aggregation change the stable population and update size?
placed.caption: Hierarchy moves the stability boundary of the sampled feedback model. (a) At $h/\tau_r=1$, each curve separates stable dynamics below it from instability above it. The orange and green bands show additional parameter ranges stabilised by a second and third aggregation layer. The $\alpha=0.35$ slice crosses at $N_c^{(1)}=138.25$, $N_c^{(2)}=217.17$ and $N_c^{(3)}=341.13$. (b) At fixed $\alpha=0.35$, increasing the update interval also raises the critical population. In both panels $\beta=0.6$, $b=1.2$ and $s=0.4$. Curves use the iterated Gaussian expected-majority model of Phases of Hierarchy~\cite{McCaul630942}, not exact small-block voting or ANF's different feedback rule. The plotted linear boundary was checked against 19,557 Jacobians, with no classification mismatch.
